judged_text: The PR rewrites the unrelated Disqus importer to route through TopicEmbed.import_remote, silently deleting the documented -c/--category option, dropping created_at preservation, and adding an unguarded network fetch of every thread link. Operators whose import scripts pass -c now fail (Thor rejects the unknown option) and every imported topic lands in uncategorized with today's timestamp instead of the thread's original date; a single dead link in the export raises OpenURI::HTTPError inside the threads loop and aborts the whole import mid-run with no resume — none of which the embed requirement asks for.

Operators whose import scripts pass -c now fail (Thor rejects the unknown option) and every imported topic lands in uncategorized with today's timestamp instead of the thread's original date; a single dead link in the export raises OpenURI::HTTPError inside the threads loop and aborts the whole import mid-run with no resume — none of which the embed requirement asks for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the code that mapped `options[:category]` to a `category_id`, so existing scripts passing `-c/--category` will now fail option parsing and imported topics can no longer be routed to a chosen category. It also replaces `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which (per `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) performs `open(url).read` without any rescue and does not pass through the original `created_at`, so a single fetch error (e.g., `OpenURI::HTTPError`) can abort the import loop and imported topics will lose their original timestamps.
